newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sundiro plans rights, B share offers.
newsitem.headline: Sundiro plans rights, B share offers.

text.p: Motorcycle producer Hainan Sundiro Motorcycle Co said on Tuesday it plans to make a 2.142-for-10 rights offer and then issue 100 million B shares in 1997.

The rights offer, tentatively priced at between four and six yuan per rights share, will be made on the firm's current total share capital of 237.44 million shares, Sundiro said in a notice in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
It said the company aims to carry out the rights issue by June 30, and plans to launch an offer of 100 million B shares in 1997 after the rights issue.

If the proposals are approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the firm will use the money raised to upgrade production technology and set up a motorcycle engine joint venture with the Japanese firm Kawasaki.
Sundiro earlier said it had signed an agreement with two Japanese firms to set up a US$29.90 million motorbike engine venture, which would be operational by the end of 1997.
Sundiro would have a 51 percent stake in the project in Haikou, capital of Hainan province, a spokesman for Sundiro told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Kawasaki will hold a 33 percent interest, with Itochu taking the remaining 16 percent, the official said.

Sundiro reported interim net earnings of 65.96 million yuan in the first half of 1996, nearly double the year-earlier level of 33.04 million yuan. Its 1995 net profits were 70.57 million yuan, up 26.4 percent on 1994's 55.83 million yuan.
Sundiro had total share capital of 169.60 million shares at the end of June of 1996, composed of 101.83 million legal person shares and 67.77 million A shares.
